business.body: ECD: 10% growth led by SDA (+30% Q4, driven by air fryers/infrared cooktops), BLDC fans (+30%+), pumps (residential share stable, agri + teens); Lighting: 14% growth, B2B shifted to higher-margin commercial, B2C moved to panels/floodlights; Butterfly: 17% revenue growth, EBIT margins stable, cash flow positive; Solar Rooftop: 5,000+ homes installed, order book Rs.500 Cr; Wires: launched as Crompton Armor in South, national rollout planned; LDA: water heater market share #2, air cooler inventory cleared
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- The deck frames a "Journey across categories" with a stated track record of entering new products and reaching leadership: pre-2016 Fans "India No.1" and "World's No.1 Ceiling Fan's Brand"; by 2023 "#3 player in Lighting", "#1 in Residential Pumps"; by 2025 "Top 3 Kitchen Brand" and "Among Fastest growing players".
- E-commerce leadership claims: "#1 Water Heaters Brand on E-com" and "#2 Air coolers in E-com".
- Categories are grouped into three tiers - Core Leadership (Fans Residential, Lighting B2C+B2B), Emerging Leadership (large domestic appliances, agri and solar pumps, kitchen appliances) and Future Build (solar rooftop, wires & cables) - with the stated strategy to "Extend leadership positions" and "Increase TAM in Right-To-Win segments" on the back of "GTM Excellence" and "Brand Legacy".
- Lighting B2B credibility is evidenced by named projects: "Google data center, NTT data center, ISRO, Tata Steel, JSW".
- Crompton 1.0 is described as "Profit led / Pole position in core categories / Successful foray into the kitchen / Innovation capability built / Extensive pan-India distribution", with Crompton 2.0 adding consumer-need-led innovation, premiumisation, supply chain excellence, GTM excellence and digital enablement.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Industry outlook] The deck cites a projected consumer durables market size of INR 3 trillion by FY29, 11% CAGR growth for the Indian consumer durable sector by 2029, 4th largest global market by 2027 and 0.9% contribution to GDP by 2027 (source: Industry Reports, IBEF).
- [Regulation] Two regulatory shifts are flagged as shaping 2026: the "BEE Ratings Upgrade", which raises manufacturing standards and is expected to "compel brands to invest in engineering and product-lifecycle practices", and "EPR Mechanisms" creating "a reverse ecosystem for sustainable, compliant product design".
- [Exceptional item] The deck's own financial tables carry an exceptional item of 716 (Rs. Cr) in the Q4 FY26 comparative column (nil in Q1 FY27 and Q1 FY26); the deck gives no explanation of what it relates to.
- [Marketing scale] Fans summer campaign reported at 80 Mn+ TV reach across 50+ channels, 52 Mn+ digital reach, 100+ billboards across 16 cities, 95 bus wraps, and 6 AI-powered in-house cricket micro-dramas with 38M+ views; Dainik Bhaskar SuperChef ran across 11 states with 36,000+ entries.
- [Awards] "Learning Reimagined Excellence of the Year 2026" award at the GEEF Global Awards.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin improved to 11.9% in Q4 from 6.8% in H1 via pricing (7-8% cumulative in fans), cost optimization (Unnati), and operating leverage; raw material inflation (post-war) partially offset by pricing; Butterfly facing similar inflation but passing on costs; no margin compression expected post-inflation normalization
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: target Rs.2,000 Cr solar business in 3-4 years; margin: sustain 10%+ EBITDA as pricing offsets inflation; order inflow: solar rooftop execution accelerating; capex/commissioning: minimal new capex, leveraging existing infrastructure for solar/wires rollout
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.500 Cr solar rooftop order book (38,000 units across Andhra & Telangana); 5,000+ homes installed; solar pumps revenue >Rs.200 Cr (doubled from prior year); wires order book not disclosed but national rollout imminent
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Rhion super-premium PL (new product line for cutting-edge design tech); national rollout of wires; Butterfly expansion into NEW markets; solar pumps & rooftop scaling to Rs.2,000 Cr business in 3-4 years; potential integration of LKA into Rhion
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Crompton delivered robust Q4 growth (11% YoY revenue, 14% lighting growth) driven by BLDC fan leadership, solar rooftop scaling (5,000+ installations), and Butterfly’s double-digit recovery, while margin expansion to 11.9% EBITDA reflected disciplined pricing and cost optimization — what matters is the strategic pivot to premiumization via Rhion and scalable new businesses (solar, wires) with strong ROCE, positioning Crompton as a multi-category consumer energy transition leader.

risks.note: Named by management as a key focus area of the Enterprise Risk Management framework. Crompton's core categories are directly exposed to BEE star-rating and efficiency labelling changes, and product roadmaps (BEE star-rated fans and water heaters) must be re-engineered whenever norms tighten.

Explicitly listed among the key risk focus areas. Quality failures would hit brand trust and warranty cost, which is why the Company embeds quality via the SAP Quality Module, stage-gate NPD validation, reliability testing, plant and supplier Kaizens and QC Story defect-reduction projects.

Flagged as a key ERM focus area. Exposure spans decarbonisation, resource efficiency, responsible product design, zero waste to landfill and monitoring of air, water and noise parameters across facilities and the supply chain, with regulatory and reputational consequences if standards slip.

Listed as a key risk focus area. Growth depends on proprietary platforms NUCLEUS (premium efficiency and BLDC-led participation) and XTECH (reliability and durability); failure to keep translating consumer insight into differentiated products would erode premiumisation and category leadership.

Named among key risk focus areas. As purchase decisions shift toward experience, after-sales support and brand credibility, weak service delivery across the retailer and service network directly threatens brand salience and repeat demand.

Management states it tracks and mitigates risks across product, brand and operational areas. Brand Crompton is the central asset behind premiumisation and go-to-market excellence, so dilution of brand salience is treated as a tracked enterprise risk.

Management identifies inventory discipline as a risk to be managed, addressed through Project ForeSight digital forecast enrichment to align production schedules with demand, standardised SOPs, rigorous vendor onboarding, Butterfly warehouse integration and QR-code Track-and-Trace across all product lines and 30 warehouses.
